summary.text: Michael Alfonso, a Republican, won the open seat for Wisconsin's 7th District on November 3, 2026, defeating Fred Clark, and will take office on January 3, 2027. He says he was raised in Vilas County and Wausau, studied mathematics at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, worked in construction and concrete, and produced The Dan Bongino Show podcast. He had not held elected office and won the August 2026 Republican primary with President Trump's endorsement.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, Alfonso was raised in Vilas County and Wausau, Wisconsin, and his grandparents fled Cuba at the end of the Castro Revolution.
He paid his own way through the University of Wisconsin-Madison by working in construction and earned a Bachelor of Science in mathematics.
He married Evita Duffy at 22 and began married life in Hayward, Wisconsin, returning to the construction and concrete industry.
About a year later, Alfonso became producer of The Dan Bongino Show podcast, according to his campaign website.
He has not held elected office.
He was endorsed by President Trump in the Republican primary; his father-in-law, Sean Duffy, held the 7th District seat until 2019.
He won the August 11, 2026 primary with 48.9% of the vote over Kevin Hermening and others and, according to WXPR before the general election, would be the youngest member of Congress if elected.
He won the November 3, 2026 general election with 56.4% of the vote to Fred Clark's 43.6%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
